newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish refinery to launch hydrocracking in July.
newsitem.headline: Polish refinery to launch hydrocracking in July.

text.p: Poland's biggest refinery expects to open a $400 million hydrocracking installation in July which would boost petrol output by 20 percent, Petrochemia Plock refinery's spokeswoman said on Friday.

Romana Kuffel told Reuters the opening of the hydrocracking installation would allow Plock to drop the production of the 94-octane leaded fuel and increase the share of 95- and 98-octane unleaded petrol to 87 percent of all produced petrol.
"In April we will open the first unit of the hydrocracking installation, the hydrogen unit, and we expect to have the whole installation working in July," Kuffel said.
She also said that at the end of November the refinery planned to open a blending installation which would allow for computer regulated blending of benzines.

Petrochemia processed about 10.5 millon tonnes of crude oil in 1996, of which petrol production accounted for some 30 percent. It expects to process 12.6 million tonnes of crude oil when it finishes the modernisation programme in 2000.
